label: Q8_0 single-row MMVQ t128 (NULL — vdr2 already wins)
rationale: Q8_0 MMVQ is the dominant kernel on Coder-30B-Q8_0 / 27B-Q8_0 decode (~80 % wall per V2.30.b). The thin-block (t128) schedule wins by ~3-5 % on Q4_0 / Q4_1 by trading occupancy ceiling for in-flight blocks-per-CU. Hypothesis: same on Q8_0.
diagnosis: vdr2 (Vector Dot product Reuse, factor 2) is already the cycle-1 productised default for Q8_0 — it doubles the per-thread inner-loop DP4A unrolling, giving better ILP per thread. t128 is a pure occupancy lever; halving the threads/block AND keeping VDR=1 throws away the ILP win that vdr2 provides. The Q4_0 / Q4_1 case is different because they were on VDR=1 baselines, so there was no ILP loss to compete against. To beat vdr2 on Q8_0 we'd need a `mmvq_q8_0_t128_vdr2` (combine both levers); not implemented this cycle.

decision.rationale: Kernel + cert ship as opt-in for future use (e.g., paired with t128_vdr2 follow-up, or for shape-specific dispatch where vdr2 might lose). Default unchanged.

follow_ups.summary: mmvq_q8_0_t128_vdr2 — combines t128 (occupancy) with VDR=2 (ILP). Likely beats both individual variants. Requires re-using vdr2 inner-loop pattern from `mmvq_q8_0_dp4a_vdr2.cu` with the t128 thread budget.
